description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Provides types supporting communication-related standards, including:
- ITU-T E.164 telephony numbers
- MIME: media types, transfer encodings, base64 and quoted-printable codecs, character sets, data: URIs, encoded words and RFC 2231 parameter values
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes:
- The packages no longer have a `net8.0` build. An application on .NET 8 or .NET 9 gets a .NET Standard build, without the APIs that only the `net10.0` build has, such as `DateOnly` and `TimeOnly` support. To keep those APIs, move the application to .NET 10.
- The `netstandard1.x` and `netstandard2.0` builds no longer list `JetBrains.Annotations` as a NuGet dependency. If your code uses its attributes and you got the package through DataStandardizer, add a reference to `JetBrains.Annotations` to your project.

New:
- `MimeMediaType` parses, formats and compares media types such as `text/plain;charset=us-ascii` (RFC 2045 §5.1), with `Suffix` (RFC 6839) and `Tree` (RFC 6838).
- `MimeParameter` holds a media type parameter's name and decoded value.
- `MimeTopLevelTypes` and `MimeMediaType` constants for the registered top-level types and common media types.
- `MimeTransferEncoding` represents a Content-Transfer-Encoding mechanism, such as `base64` or an `x-` extension, with `IsIdentity` and `Domain` (`MimeDataDomain`) to tell what data a transport must carry.
- `MimeBase64Encoder` and `MimeBase64Decoder` encode and decode base64 buffer by buffer, as the RFC 2045 `base64` Content-Transfer-Encoding (`MimeBase64Mode.Mime`) or the strict RFC 4648 form of iCalendar BINARY values and RFC 2047 "B" encoded words (`MimeBase64Mode.Strict`); `MimeBase64` has one-shot and length methods.
- `MimeQuotedPrintableEncoder` and `MimeQuotedPrintableDecoder` encode and decode quoted-printable buffer by buffer, as the RFC 2045 `quoted-printable` Content-Transfer-Encoding (`MimeQuotedPrintableMode.Body`) or the RFC 2047 "Q" encoding of encoded words in text, comment or phrase context; `MimeQuotedPrintable` has one-shot and length methods and `EndsWithSoftLineBreak`.
- Add MimeCharset and MimeCharsetResolver for character set names and their encodings.
- Add MimeDataUri for RFC 2397 data: URIs.
- `MimeMediaType` decodes RFC 2231 parameter sections and extended values (character set and language), and rejects anything RFC 2231 doesn't allow unless the caller opts in with a `MimeMediaTypeParseOptions` member: `AllowMissingSections`, `AllowDuplicateSections` and `AllowLeadingZeroSectionNumbers` (together, `AllowNonstandardSections`), `AllowQuotedExtendedValues` and `AllowLowercaseHexDigits` (together, `AllowNonstandardExtendedValues`), `AllowUnknownCharsets` and `AllowInvalidOctets`.
- `MimeParameter` takes values that aren't US-ASCII and an optional RFC 1766 language, writes them as RFC 2231 extended values, and splits long parameters into sections with `FormatSections`.
- `MimeEncodedWord` reads and writes RFC 2047 encoded words in header text, with RFC 2231 languages; `EncodeText` writes text as encoded words and `DecodeText` decodes a run of text, with `MimeEncodedWordParseOptions` opt-ins for words that don't follow the rules.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber` has `==` and `!=` operators.

Fixed:
- TelephonyInfo.CurrentTelephony no longer throws when the current culture is the invariant culture.
- On netstandard1.1, RFC 2231 parameter values whose octets aren't valid in their character set are no longer accepted unless `AllowInvalidOctets` is given.
- The `netstandard1.1` build depends on `System.Net.Http` 4.3.4 instead of 4.3.2, which has a known vulnerability.
- Debuggers can step into the packages' source through Source Link.
- Accept raw UTF-8 in a quoted Content-Type parameter value (RFC 6532 §3.2).
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber` values that are equal have the same hash code, and `Equals(object)` agrees with `Equals(ItuE164InternationalNumber)`, so hash-based collections find equal numbers.
- TelephonyInfo country constructors load the number format for that country, not the invariant one.
- ItuE164InternationalNumber.Parse and TryParse reject more than 15 digits when the international prefix symbol is not allowed.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.Parse` and `TryParse` reject leading white space unless `AllowLeadingWhite` is set, and a final line feed unless `AllowTrailingWhite` is set.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.Parse` and `TryParse` no longer treat control characters other than U+0009 to U+000D as white space or as separators.
- A utf-16 or utf-32 decoder from MimeCharsetResolver looks for a byte order mark again after a flush.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.ToString(format, provider)` and `ToString(provider)` format the number, not the type name, when the provider is `null` or a `CultureInfo`, so `string.Format` with a culture formats it too.
- TelephonyInfo.CurrentTelephony gives the default instance for a culture whose region is a UN M.49 code.
- The network `IdentificationCode` and `SubscriberNumber` of an `ItuE164InternationalNumber` throw `InvalidOperationException`, not `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`, when the number ends inside its identification code.
- The invariant `i` and `I` formats of `ItuE164InternationalNumber` write the international prefix symbol `+` and the whole Country Code, such as `+44 3071234567`, instead of a literal `p` and only the first digit of the Country Code.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.ToString` formats a `null`, empty or white-space format as the default `G` format, instead of returning an empty string, so `string.Format("{0}", number)` and `$"{number}"` print the number.
- The ulong E.164 factories reject a number without an assigned Country Code or Identification Code.
- The typed E.164 factories reject a National Significant Number or Subscriber Number with no digits.

Changed:
- The netstandard1.x and netstandard2.0 builds now carry nullable annotations, so projects on C# 8 or later with nullable enabled get null warnings from them.
- MimeBase64Encoder encodes MIME lines about ten times faster on .NET 10.
- MimeBase64.TryDecode and Decode allocate one array for padded data.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.ToString` returns an empty string, not the type name, when a format provider's own formatter returns `null`.
- `ItuE164InternationalNumber.ToString` reads a format longer than one character as a custom pattern, even when it begins with `g`, `G`, `i` or `I`.
